correctness.rationale: For m>=1, a=floor(log2(m)), L=a+1, each input residue r mod 2^L has one uniquely closest root j* among 0..m-1, strictly larger in 2-adic distance valuation than all other roots. The product-difference telescoping formula isolates a uniquely minimal-valuation summand, proving exact branch isometry depth d=L+sum_{i!=j*}nu_2(r-i)-nu_2(m!). For lower index 2m and input 2r+epsilon, the nearest root is 2j*+epsilon; the depth is the same by nu_2((2m)!)=m+nu_2(m!). Equality of binomial valuations and the bound nu_2(B_m(r))>=d-1 make the branch image centers identical mod 2^d. Thus both branches biject onto the same output ball; branch inverses compose into a global class-preserving bijective isometry. Exact finite computation through m=32 for branch quantities and through m=24,k=6 for full histograms yielded 30,890 passing checks. Computation is supplemental; the proof is not inductive extrapolation.

value.rationale: The lower-index doubling map gives an exact structural invariance for every positive column, every dyadic depth and each input residue ball, via globally defined 2-adic isometries. It collapses infinitely many apparently separate residue-fiber distribution problems into one problem per odd lower-index value, preserves nonuniform laws such as the fifth-column distribution along its full doubling orbit, and yields an explicit all-depth local conjugacy rather than a routine valuation corollary. This is a mathematically motivated, reusable identity with no reliance on finite enumeration for the proof.
